text:
jordan: FYI customer zephyr-inc says audit export to their Splunk forwarder is missing ~20m of events for 2026-01-12 02:00-02:20 UTC. Manifest lists several zero-byte chunks under tenant-zephyr. S3 path: s3://audit-exports/tenant-zephyr/2026/01/12/02/manifest-0003.json. Can anyone quickly check KMS/HSM or forwarder errors?

maria: Are those zero-byte entries real files or placeholders? Can you paste a manifest excerpt + any forwarder log lines? Also confirm if this tenant uses HSM-backed keys or standard KMS alias.

jordan: Manifest excerpt:
```
{
  "chunk_id": "c-0003-12",
  "size_bytes": 0,
  "s3_key": "tenant-zephyr/2026/01/12/02/c-0003-12.avro",
  "status": "stored",
  "notes": "zero-byte, upload reported success"
}
```
No explicit error in manifest. Forwarder log (truncated):
```
2026-01-12T02:05:12Z forwarder[pid=123]: upload succeeded: c-0002-11 (2048 bytes)
2026-01-12T02:07:03Z forwarder[pid=123]: upload succeeded: c-0003-12 (0 bytes)
2026-01-12T02:07:04Z forwarder[pid=123]: EncryptFailed: KMSInvalidCiphertextException: Invalid ciphertext
```

ashok: KMSInvalidCiphertextException usually means someone re-encrypted or rotated alias and ciphertext doesn't match new key. Did we rotate alias/redwood-audit-tenant-zephyr recently? Also check if forwarder re-encrypt step is running with the correct key id.

maria: I recall a partial alias rotation yesterday for tenants using customer-managed keys. Jordan, can you run rapid checks: 1) aws kms list-aliases --key-id alias/redwood-audit-tenant-zephyr 2) check forwarder IAM role for kms:Decrypt on the new key 3) head-object on that s3 key to confirm content present.

jordan: Ran head-object, object exists but size reported 0. KMS list-aliases shows alias pointing to arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abcd-rotated. Forwarder role policy currently references old key ARN.

sre-bot: export-job-78123 warning: some chunks flagged zero-bytes; auto-reenqueue disabled for rotated-key mismatch.

ashok: Ok, root cause looks like alias rotation without updating forwarder role/key usage. Steps: 1) grant forwarder role kms:Decrypt on new key OR add a grant/alias mapping for backward compat 2) run reencrypt-backfill playbook to re-encrypt zero-byte (corrupt) objects or replay raw events into fresh chunks 3) confirm SIEM-forwarder checksum parity after backfill. Quick mitigation: enable fallback-key in forwarder to the previous key (if still available) to allow decryption and re-upload.

maria: For the customer-facing note: explain we detected alias rotation and permission mismatch; we will update forwarder key permissions and run a limited backfill for the affected 02:00-02:20 window. ETA ~3 hours for small backfill, will update if longer.

jordan: I started a ticket with infra to add kms:Decrypt for forwarder role on new key and kicked off a diagnostic replay for tenant-zephyr 02:00-02:30. I'll post logs here once backfill completes. :eyes: 

ashok: After backfill, run these checks: 1) verify manifest sizes >0 2) confirm forwarder exit codes are 0 3) test Splunk ingestion for a sample chunk 4) if any objects still show zero bytes, run s3 cp to local and inspect encryption headers.

maria: Adding action items: @infra to update KMS policy, @support to notify customer of planned backfill window, @ops to monitor SIEM ingest.

jordan: On it — tagging infra and support, will update thread when backfill finishes.
